provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Culture and greetings
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify Nigerian greetings.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate greetings in Yoruba.

Introduction:
We greet people every day. Today we learn how to greet the Nigerian way.

Content:
In Yoruba culture we say "Ekaaro" for good morning. Hausa people say "Inna lillahi" for hello. Igbo people say "Nno" for welcome. Different cultures have different ways to greet.

Class activity:
Let's practice these greetings. I will call out a culture and you will respond with the right greeting.

Evaluation questions:
What do we say in Yoruba for good morning?
How do Hausa people greet?
What does Igbo greeting mean?

Summary:
We learned three Nigerian greetings today.

topics.title: National anthem and pledge
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite the national pledge.
The pupils should be able to sing the first stanza of the national anthem.

Introduction:
We love our country Nigeria. We show this by singing our anthem and saying our pledge.

Content:
The pledge says "I pledge to Nigeria my country" and more. The anthem starts "Nigeria we hail thee". We stand straight when singing or saying them.

Class activity:
Let's practice the pledge together. We will stand tall and speak clearly.

Evaluation questions:
What comes first in the pledge?
What is the first line of the anthem?
When do we sing the anthem?

Summary:
We learned how to say our pledge and sing our anthem.

topics.title: Our national colours
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify the national colours.
The pupils should be able to draw the Nigerian flag.

Introduction:
Our country has special colours. Today we learn about our national flag.

Content:
The Nigerian flag has three colours. Green stands for agriculture. White stands for peace. The flag is green-white-green. We see it at important places.

Class activity:
Let's colour our own flag. We will use green and white crayons.

Evaluation questions:
What are the colours of our flag?
What does green stand for?
What does white stand for?

Summary:
We learned about our national flag colours.

topics.title: Community helpers 1
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify a teacher and doctor.
The pupils should be able to state how teachers help us.

Introduction:
Many people help us in our community. Today we learn about teachers and doctors.

Content:
A teacher helps us learn in school. A doctor helps us when we are sick. Teachers teach us to read and write. Doctors give us medicine to feel better.

Class activity:
Let's play a game. I will say what a helper does and you say who helps us.

Evaluation questions:
Who teaches us in school?
Who helps us when we are sick?
How does a teacher help us?

Summary:
We learned about teachers and doctors who help us.

topics.title: Community helpers 2
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify a police officer and firefighter.
The pupils should be able to explain how police keep us safe.

Introduction:
Some community helpers keep us safe. Today we learn about police and firefighters.

Content:
A police officer wears uniform and directs traffic. A firefighter puts out fires. Police catch bad people. Firefighters rescue people from burning buildings.

Class activity:
Let's pretend to be police officers. We will direct traffic in our classroom.

Evaluation questions:
What does a police officer wear?
What does a firefighter do?
Who catches bad people?

Summary:
We learned about police and firefighters who keep us safe.

topics.title: Market day manners
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to greet a market trader.
The pupils should be able to use please and thank you when buying.

Introduction:
When we go to the market we must be polite. Today we learn market manners.

Content:
We greet the trader first. We say "good morning" or "good afternoon". We say "please" when we ask for something. We say "thank you" when we get it.

Class activity:
Let's practice buying things in the market. I will be the trader and you will be the customer.

Evaluation questions:
What do we say first when we meet a trader?
What magic word do we use when asking?
What do we say after we get what we want?

Summary:
We learned to be polite when buying things at the market.

topics.title: Transport manners
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to demonstrate sitting properly in a car.
The pupils should be able to identify safe behaviour in transport.

Introduction:
When we travel in cars we must be safe. Today we learn transport manners.

Content:
We sit in the car seat. We wear the seat belt. We do not stand when the car is moving. We do not wave our hands out of the window.

Class activity:
Let's pretend we are in a car. We will show how to sit properly.

Evaluation questions:
What must we wear in the car?
Can we stand when the car moves?
Can we wave from the window?

Summary:
We learned how to behave safely in a car.

topics.title: Visiting manners
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to knock before entering a room.
The pupils should be able to greet a host properly.

Introduction:
When we visit people's houses we must be polite. Today we learn visiting manners.

Content:
We knock on the door before entering. We greet the host with a smile. We sit nicely on the chair. We do not touch things without asking.

Class activity:
Let's practice visiting a friend. We will knock and greet properly.

Evaluation questions:
What do we do before entering a room?
How do we greet the host?
How should we sit when visiting?

Summary:
We learned how to be good visitors.

topics.title: Helping the community
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify littering as bad behaviour.
The pupils should be able to state ways to keep the environment clean.

Introduction:
We must keep our community clean. Today we learn how to help our community.

Content:
We do not throw rubbish on the street. We use the bin. We keep our school and estate clean. When we see litter, we pick it up.

Class activity:
Let's make posters about keeping our environment clean.

Evaluation questions:
Is it good to throw rubbish on the street?
Where should we put our litter?
How can we help keep our school clean?

Summary:
We learned how to help keep our community clean.

topics.title: Revision and community day
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to dress as a community helper.
The pupils should be able to explain what a community helper does.

Introduction:
We have learned about many community helpers. Today we celebrate them.

Content:
We will dress up as our favorite community helper. We will say what our helper does. We will sing songs about helping others.

Class activity:
Let's dress up as community helpers. We will parade and tell what our helper does.

Evaluation questions:
Who did you dress up as?
What does your community helper do?
Why are community helpers important?

Summary:
We celebrated all the community helpers who help us.
